Linear with your GitHub account will extend Linear's capabilities by linking pull requests to Linear issues and automatically advance the status of linked issues when pull requests are created and landed.

**Connect GitHub:** [https://linear.app/settings/integrations/github](https://linear.app/settings/integrations/github)

### Tips

**You can reference Linear issues in GitHub by:**

* **Branch name** (e.g. LIN-123 or username/LIN-123). 

  To quickly copy branch name for an issue to your clipboard, press `cmd` `shift` `.`
* **Pull request title** (e.g. GitHub Workflow LIN-123)
* **Pull request description or comment** (e.g. *Fixes LIN-123, Resolver LIN-123*)

**When you reference a Linear issue in GitHub, Linear will:**

* Add a link to the GitHub PR link to the Linear issue.
* Comment on the GitHub PR with a link back to the Linear issue.
* Once PR has been opened, Linear will change the status of the issue to "In Progress".
* Once PR has been merged, Linear will change the status of the issue as "Done".

**GitHub Workflow**

1. Select or create the issue you want to work on next.
2. Open the command menu (`Cmd` `K` on Mac, or `Ctrl` `K` on Windows) and select **Copy git branch name,** or use the shortcut `cmd` `shift` `.`
3. This will copy the git branch name to your clipboard (e.g. username/LIN-123-github-workflow)
4. Paste the branch name to your git checkout command to create a new branch: **git checkout -b username/LIN-123-github-workflow**
5. Make your changes and push the branch to GitHub and open a pull request
6. Once the pull request is open, Linear will comment on the PR and change the issue state to **In Progress***.* 
7. Once the PR merged, Linear will change the status to Done.

When you're done with this issue, you can archive it via the command menu or by using the keyboard shortcut `#`.
